newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close weaker, secondaries flat.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close weaker, secondaries flat.

text.p: Malaysian stocks closed practically unchanged in thinner trading than recent sessions.
The Composite Index was down 0.31 point at 1134.96, while the Second Board Index rose 0.86 at 568.45. The all-share Emas index fell 0.25 at 329.72.

"Fund managers have been selectively accumulating infrastructure-related stocks," said John Engle, managing director of brokers HG Asia in Kuala Lumpur. "The foreign funds have been quieter today," he added.
Total volume stood at 191 million against 223 million on Monday. Losers outpaced gainers 347 to 233.
"Stocks like Gamuda, UEM and Sungei Way are all near their all-time highs on demand for toll-roads," said Engle.

Gamuda was up 70 cents at 19.40 after hitting an intra-day high of 19.60, and closing at a new high for the year. UEM was unchanged at 19.40, also at its year high, while Sungei Way was up 10 cents at 13.50, 10 cents below its year high.
Aokam was down 16 at 4.02 after posting a massive 145 million ringgit loss for the year ended June 30 1996.
"It's surprising how little it moved, considering the results," said Engle. "It's obvious that someone was picking up the stock," he added.
